---
title: "Iteration"
---
## Goals of this notebook

This notebook is a demo of an iterative process for adding new court data releases without redoing manual work. It follows the same order as the cleaning and analysis notebooks.

1. Configure project constants in one place
2. Import every release found in `data-raw/`
3. Merge releases and remove duplicates (keeping the most recent release)
4. Geocode only addresses that have never been geocoded
5. Apply saved OpenRefine decisions (crosswalks) and flag anything new for review
6. Fix dates and create flags
7. Validate and export clean data
8. Compare the new clean data to the previous release
9. Analysis: compute numbers instead of typing them
## R Markdown


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)

## Importing and cleaning names

# finds every data set in data-raw, so a new one is picked up automatically
raw_files <- list.files("data-raw",
                        pattern = "^unhoused-raw-\\d+\\.xlsx$",
                        full.names = TRUE)

# does everything we used to do one data set at a time
read_unhoused <- function(file) {
  unhoused_raw <- suppressWarnings(read_excel(file))

  unhoused_names <- unhoused_raw |>
    clean_names() |>
    rename(any_of(c(
      defendant_address = "defendent_address",               
      total_fine_amount_due = "totla_fine_amount_due",       
      total_fine_amount_paid = "totla_fine_amount_paid",     
      total_fine_amount_dismissed = "totla_fine_amount_dismissed",
      phone_number = "defendant_phone_number"              
    )))

  unhoused_names |>
    mutate(phone_number = as.character(phone_number), 
           data_origin = paste0("unhoused_", str_extract(basename(file), "\\d+"))) # unhoused_1, unhoused_2...
}

unhoused_list <- map(raw_files, read_unhoused)

## Merging data sets 

unhoused_merged <- bind_rows(unhoused_list)

if (n_distinct(map_int(unhoused_list, ncol)) > 1 |
    ncol(unhoused_merged) != ncol(unhoused_list[[1]])) {
  stop("The columns in one of the data sets don't match. Run glimpse() on each one and add a rename() to read_unhoused().")
}

## Remove duplicate rows

unhoused_no_dupes <- unhoused_merged |>
  arrange(desc(as.numeric(str_extract(data_origin, "\\d+")))) |> 
  distinct(across(!c(
    data_origin,
    defendant_address)),
    .keep_all = TRUE)

## Geocoding

# Reformatting addresses to geocode externally using geocodio
unhoused_reformatted <- unhoused_no_dupes |>
  mutate(full_address = paste(str_remove(offense_location, ","),
                              "Houston, TX", sep = ", "))

geocoded_files <- list.files("data-processed",
                             pattern = "^unhoused-geocoded-\\d+\\.csv$",
                             full.names = TRUE)

geocoded_addresses <- map(geocoded_files, read_csv, col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  clean_names() |> 
  select(full_address, starts_with("geocodio")) |>
  distinct(full_address, .keep_all = TRUE)

unhoused_to_geocode <- unhoused_reformatted |>
  filter(!full_address %in% geocoded_addresses$full_address)

# Exporting the new rows to geocode in geocodio
next_number <- length(geocoded_files) + 1

if (nrow(unhoused_to_geocode) > 0) {
  write_csv(unhoused_to_geocode,
            paste0("data-processed/unhoused-to-geocode-", next_number, ".csv"))
}


```
